To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain is an immune privileged site and that adenovirus-mediated gene transfer to the brain is not affected by pre-existing immunity.
systemic anti-Ad vector immunity is not a major factor limiting the efficacy of Ad vector gene therapy within the brain.
systemic anti-Ad vector immune responses do not affect Ad vector gene therapy of intracerebral tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of replication deficient adenovirus vectors to deliver genes into the brain for the purpose of treating malignant glioma.
the development of adenoviral vector based gene therapy strategies for the treatment of human brain tumors.
understanding the mechanisms that limit the effectiveness of gene therapy in brain tumors and developing strategies to circumvent these limitations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune response to Ad.CMV-betagl in the CNS is significantly less than in the periphery.
adenoviruses are not immunogenic in the central nervous system, but that the central nervous system is not immunologically inert.
the CNS is an immune privileged site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the brain is a relatively immune privileged site and therefore, adenoviruses may be used for gene therapy in the central nervous system without the concern of immune responses.

the immune response to adenoviral vector administration in the brain is significantly attenuated when compared to that seen after systemic vector administration and that the central nervous system may represent an immunologically privileged site.
we have demonstrated that intracerebral administration of adenoviral vectors can be repeated with minimal or no effect on subsequent transgene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central nervous system may be more immunologically protected than previously thought.
adenoviral vector-mediated gene therapy is an effective strategy for the treatment of glioblastoma.
the immune system can be manipulated to improve the efficacy and duration of gene therapy for brain tumors.
